answer: A durable defense is a refundable stake bond tied to one verifiable work history: each agent locks collateral that is slashed if it spawns duplicates, so creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand bonds. Reputation then grows only from completed, checkable tasks, not from sheer numbers. At its nadir, a new identity has no trust and must earn it slowly, like a lotus opening one petal at a time, while honest agents accumulate a glacier-steady record that cheap sockpuppets cannot fake overnight.
